title: Collector state machine, fallback behavior, and SIEM batch-retry guidance
content:
Summary:
This doc captures the proposed lightweight state machine for evidence records as they flow through collector & orchestrator components, the recommended fallback and backfill behavior for collector-side failures, and a concrete batch/retry format for SIEM export (NDJSON envelope + watermarking). Goal is to be pragmatic: avoid heavy-weight distributed transactions while preserving forensic integrity, auditability, and efficient SIEM consumption.

Why this matters (context):
- We need predictable semantics for evidence transitions to support control audits, incident forensics, and automated retention/TTL.
- Collectors operate at the edge and may be flaky; collectors must be allowed to retry safely without duplicating evidence in SIEMs or breaking provenance.
- SIEM exports are batched for throughput. We need an idempotent, signed, watermark-based export envelope and clear retry rules.

Scope:
- Applies to: edge collectors (sidecar & agent), evidence-orchestrator, export workers, SIEM adapter/ingest.
- Not in scope: downstream SIEM internals, long-term archival policies beyond retention TTLs (covered elsewhere).

High-level state machine (for an evidence item):
- RECEIVED: initial state when a collector accepts a payload (assigns evidence_id, local seq).
- VALIDATED: schema and token-level RBAC checked; non-retryable errors move to REJECTED.
- NORMALIZED: fields normalized, pseudonymization applied if required.
- QUEUED_FOR_EXPORT: ready to be batched for SIEM/export.
- EXPORTING: currently in an outbound batch being transmitted.
- EXPORTED: acknowledged by downstream (adapter returns 200 + envelope_id).
- ARCHIVED: moved to long-term store per retention policy (after EXPORTED or tombstone window).
- FAILED_RETRYABLE: transient failure logged; will be retried with backoff.
- FAILED_PERMANENT / REJECTED: unrecoverable or policy rejections (kept as tombstone/metadata for audit).

Notes on transitions and guarantees:
- Evidence_id: UUIDv4 assigned at RECEIVED. Collectors MUST include an idempotency_key header equal to evidence_id on any retry traffic.
- Transition semantics are eventual: we provide at-least-once delivery semantics to the orchestrator and best-effort exactly-once to SIEM via envelope+watermark and dedupe on downstream.
- For fast failure detection, a transition to FAILED_RETRYABLE should include failure_code and retry_after_ms.
- Permanent failure (schema mismatch, banned content) => move to REJECTED with reason, redact payload per compliance, keep metadata for chain-of-custody.

Collector behavior (sidecar/agent):
- On network or auth failure when sending to orchestrator, collector will retry with exponential backoff: base 500ms, factor 2, max 2m, jitter 0.2. Cap retries at N_attempts=8 before falling back to local disk queue with tombstone timer.
- Local disk queue is bounded by disk_quota and uses LRU eviction of non-essential telemetry; evidence items must never be silently dropped without a logged tombstone event.
- If local queue grows past high_water_mark (default 80% of quota), emit alert to SRE channel and start backpressure (respond 429 to upstream services until cleared).
- On restart, collector replays queued items preserving evidence_id and original_created_at. Replayed items must include replay=true header.

Replay and duplicate detection:
- Orchestrator maintains a short-term dedupe cache keyed on evidence_id (TTL default 24h). Duplicate submissions with matching evidence_id are ignored (ack returned) but audit trail notes "duplicate-replay" with origin collector id.

SIEM batch export envelope (NDJSON):
- Use NDJSON where each line is a compact JSON object (no nested objects beyond simple maps). Export worker builds an envelope file per target SIEM ingest: envelope metadata + items.
- Envelope header (single JSON line) fields (all strings unless noted):
  - envelope_id: UUIDv4
  - target: SIEM-name or sink-id
  - produced_at: ISO8601
  - batch_sequence: integer (stringified)
  - min_event_time: ISO8601 of earliest item
  - max_event_time: ISO8601 of latest item
  - watermark: base64(HMAC_SHA256(sorted(list of evidence_id)) ) -> used for quick integrity check
  - signer_id: collector/orchestrator id that signed this envelope
  - signature: base64(signature of canonicalized envelope header)
  - item_count: integer (stringified)
- Following header, each subsequent line is an item with fields: evidence_id, event_time, origin_collector_id, schema_version, normalized_payload (stringified small JSON), provenance (short map), redaction_marker boolean, checksum_sha256.
- Example NDJSON lines (one-line examples) are included in the appendix (see below).

Batch size and timing heuristics:
- Default max envelope size: 5MB; item_count_limit: 2000; max_interval: 60s.
- Workers flush early if envelope approaches size limit, or memory pressure is detected.

Retry semantics for export workers:
- On transient upstream failure (5xx or 429), use exponential backoff with jitter: base 1s, factor 2, max 5m, max_attempts 10.
- On auth failure (401/403): fail fast, mark envelope as FAILED_PERMANENT, emit alert to security team, do not retry until operator fixes credentials.
- Important: All retries MUST be idempotent. Envelopes are immutable; each attempt uses same envelope_id and signature. Downstream dedupe should use envelope_id + item checksums.

Watermarking and integrity checks:
- Use watermark (HMAC over ordered evidence_ids) to detect accidental shuffles or partial uploads across multiple envelopes. If two envelopes for same batch_sequence have mismatched watermarks, mark both for manual reconciliation.
- Keep per-target last_applied_batch_sequence to avoid applying older batches out-of-order. Export worker must increment sequence monotonically and persist sequence state atomically to ensure monotonicity across restarts.

Backfill and collector-side patching plan (short notes):
- When ingest backfill is needed (e.g., collector was offline for 12h), orchestrator creates a backfill job with backfill_window {start, end} and a backfill_marker boolean set on each replayed item.
- Backfill batches use a separate prefix in sequence numbers (e.g., backfill-20251103-<n>) so downstream can apply special recon ingestion paths or metadata.
- Backfill jobs must not retroactively update already-EXPORTED items — rather, they should be appended with explicit backfill_marker and reconciled in the SIEM via correlation on evidence_id.

Observability, metrics & alerts (minimum):
- Metrics exposed: received_count, validated_count, normalized_count, queued_size, export_success_count, export_fail_count, export_retry_count, duplicate_replay_count, local_queue_size, disk_quota_exhausted_count.
- Traces: sample 1/100 requests through collector->orchestrator->export with trace tags: evidence_id, envelope_id, batch_sequence.
- Alerts: local_queue%>80 -> paging; export_fail_rate > 5% over 10m -> paging; sequence_gap_detected -> paging to SRE + security.

Audit trail & RBAC notes:
- Evidence metadata must include a token_affinity field (which API token/client_id produced the event) to enable per-token audit and RBAC provenance checks.
- Only a small RBAC-privileged subset can view raw payloads. Access to raw payloads must be logged as an "evidence-access" audit event and included in the long-term audit index.

Security considerations (short):
- All envelope payloads in-flight must be TLS 1.2+ and signed. Signatures use rotating keys stored in KMS; signer_id maps to key version.
- Sensitive fields must be redacted or pseudonymized at NORMALIZED stage unless explicitly allowed by config (with a documented business justification).

Appendix: Example NDJSON (3-line excerpt)
{"envelope_id":"b3c4f2d8-9a2f-4d1c-a8b2-1b4c22f7a001","target":"splunk-us-east","produced_at":"2026-02-28T14:21:05Z","batch_sequence":"1528","min_event_time":"2026-02-28T14:20:00Z","max_event_time":"2026-02-28T14:21:00Z","watermark":"c2hhMjU2aGFzaCJ9","signer_id":"orch-worker-07","signature":"MEUCIQDA...","item_count":"3"}
{"evidence_id":"9f1b6f8a-3c9a-4c44-b1ac-2e4d4e93a77e","event_time":"2026-02-28T14:20:12Z","origin_collector_id":"collector-eu-2","schema_version":"v2.1","normalized_payload":"{\"event\":\"user-login\",\"user_id_hashed\":\"h_123abc\"}","provenance":"{src:agent,proto:http}","redaction_marker":"false","checksum_sha256":"af0c..."}
{"evidence_id":"a7d4b5cc-2a22-4f5e-9f0b-8d8aeadb12c3","event_time":"2026-02-28T14:20:33Z","origin_collector_id":"collector-eu-2","schema_version":"v2.1","normalized_payload":"{\"event\":\"config-change\",\"actor\":\"svc-deploy\"}","provenance":"{src:agent,proto:http}","redaction_marker":"true","checksum_sha256":"d4e2..."}

Operational checklist before launching to prod for a new SIEM target:
- [ ] Confirm envelope signing key provisioning in KMS + signer mapping in config.
- [ ] Update orch worker env with target endpoint + credentials; validate 200 semantics.
- [ ] Set sequence store (etcd/postgres) and run a failover test.
- [ ] Run full end-to-end test with backfill payloads and duplicate-replay cases.
- [ ] Verify retention TTLs and archival job runs on a dry-run.

Open questions / proposals for follow-up:
- Should dedupe cache TTL be longer than 24h for low-throughput tenants? tradeoff: memory vs safer dedupe.
- How should we represent partial redactions in normalized_payload while keeping checksum stability? proposal: canonicalize to redaction placeholders before checksumming.
- Do we want a lightweight signed checkpoint ACK from SIEM beyond 200/202 to simplify reconciliation? (Pros: stronger guarantees. Cons: operational complexity).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic — please flag any forensic/regulatory gaps.
- If you care about a specific downstream SIEM (Splunk/Elastic/QRadar), add a note so we can add sink-specific adapters (e.g., field mappings).
